sentences.cn_text: 这些工具能够帮助你赢得每一场争论——不是以击败对手这种无益的方式,而是以更好的方式去了解分歧所在,了解他们为何与我们持不同意见,并学会如何与他们对话和协作。
sentences.en_text: These tools can help you win every argument — not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people, learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them.

sentences.cn_text: 如果我们重新审视对争论的看法——从口头争斗或网球比赛转变为一种理性交流,通过这种交流我们都能获得相互尊重和理解——那么我们就改变了「赢得」争论的本质含义。
sentences.en_text: If we readjust our view of arguments — from a verbal fight or tennis game to a reasoned exchange through which we all gain mutual respect and understanding — then we change the very nature of what it means to “win” an argument.

sentences.cn_text: 当然,许多讨论并非都如此成功。
sentences.en_text: Of course, many discussions are not so successful.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管如此,我们仍需谨慎,不要过快地指责对手提出了糟糕的论点。
sentences.en_text: Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly.

sentences.cn_text: 我们需要学会如何正确评估这些论点。
sentences.en_text: We need to learn how to evaluate them properly.

sentences.cn_text: 评估的很大一部分工作是指出糟糕的论点,但我们也需要承认对手的优秀论点,并对自己适用同样的批判性标准。
sentences.en_text: A large part of evaluation is calling out bad arguments, but we also need to admit good arguments by opponents and to apply the same critical standards to ourselves.

sentences.cn_text: 谦逊要求你认识到自己论点中的弱点,有时也要接受对立面的理由。
sentences.en_text: Humility requires you to recognize weaknesses in your own arguments and sometimes also to accept reasons on the opposite side.

sentences.cn_text: 这一切都并非易事,但即使他人拒绝,你也可以开始行动。
sentences.en_text: None of this will be easy, but you can start even if others refuse to.

sentences.cn_text: 下次你陈述自己的立场时,为你的主张构建一个论证,并诚实地问自己这个论证是否站得住脚。
sentences.en_text: Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and honestly ask yourself whether your argument is any good.

sentences.cn_text: 下次你与持有某种立场的人交谈时,请他们为自己的观点提供理由。
sentences.en_text: Next time you talk with someone who takes a stand, ask them to give you a reason for their view.

sentences.cn_text: 完整而善意地阐述他们的论证。
sentences.en_text: Spell out their argument fully and charitably.

sentences.cn_text: 公正地评估其强度。
sentences.en_text: Assess its strength impartially.

sentences.cn_text: 提出反对意见并认真倾听他们的回应。
sentences.en_text: Raise objections and listen carefully to their replies.

sentences.cn_text: 如果争论是战斗,卡内基的说法就是对的,而我们通常也正是这样看待争论的。
sentences.en_text: Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them.

sentences.cn_text: 就像身体上的打斗一样,言语上的争斗也会让双方都伤痕累累。
sentences.en_text: Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied.

sentences.cn_text: 即使你赢了,你的境况也不会变得更好。
sentences.en_text: Even when you win, you end up no better off.

sentences.cn_text: 如果争论仅仅是竞赛——比如说网球比赛——你的前景也几乎同样黯淡。
sentences.en_text: Your prospects would be almost as dismal if arguments were even just competitions — like, say, tennis games.

sentences.cn_text: 对手双方将球来回击打,直到从所有参与者中产生一位胜者。
sentences.en_text: Pairs of opponents hit the ball back and forth until one winner emerges from all who entered.

sentences.cn_text: 其他所有人都是失败者。
sentences.en_text: Everybody else loses.

sentences.cn_text: 正是这种思维方式导致许多人试图回避争论,尤其是关于政治和宗教的争论。
sentences.en_text: This kind of thinking is why so many people try to avoid arguments, especially about politics and religion.

sentences.cn_text: 戴尔·卡内基在1936年的著作《人性的弱点》中写道:「只有一种方法能在争论中获得最佳结果——那就是避免争论。」这种对争论的反感很常见,但它建立在对争论的错误认识之上,这种认识给我们的个人和社会生活带来了深刻的问题——并且在许多方面背离了争论的初衷。
sentences.en_text: In his 1936 work How to Win Friends and Influence People, Dale Carnegie wrote: “There is only one way... to get the best of an argument — and that is to avoid it.” This aversion to arguments is common, but it depends on a mistaken view of arguments that causes profound problems for our personal and social lives — and in many ways misses the point of arguing in the first place.

sentences.cn_text: 这些关于争论的看法也削弱了理性。
sentences.en_text: These views of arguments also undermine reason.

sentences.cn_text: 如果你把对话视为一场战斗或竞赛,只要不被发现,你就可以通过作弊获胜。
sentences.en_text: If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don’t get caught.

sentences.cn_text: 你会乐于用糟糕的论点去说服他人。
sentences.en_text: You will be happy to convince people with bad arguments.

sentences.cn_text: 你可以称他们的观点愚蠢,或拿他们的无知开玩笑。
sentences.en_text: You can call their views stupid, or joke about how ignorant they are.

sentences.cn_text: 这些伎俩都无助于你理解他们、他们的立场或你们之间的分歧,但它们确实能在某种意义上帮你获胜。
sentences.en_text: None of these tricks will help you understand them, their positions or the issues that divide you, but they can help you win — in one way.

sentences.cn_text: 有一种更好的方式来赢得争论。
sentences.en_text: There is a better way to win arguments.

sentences.cn_text: 假设你支持提高本州的最低工资,而我反对。
sentences.en_text: Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not.

sentences.cn_text: 如果你大喊「赞成」,而我大喊「反对」,我们谁都学不到任何东西。
sentences.en_text: If you yell, “Yes,” and I yell, “No,” neither of us learns anything.

sentences.cn_text: 我们既不理解也不尊重对方,也没有妥协或合作的基础。
sentences.en_text: We neither understand nor respect each other, and we have no basis for compromise or cooperation.

sentences.cn_text: 相反,假设你提出一个合理的论证:全职工作者不应该生活在贫困之中。
sentences.en_text: In contrast, suppose you give a reasonable argument: that full-time workers should not have to live in poverty.

sentences.cn_text: 然后我提出另一个合理的论证:更高的最低工资会迫使企业雇佣更少的员工并缩短工作时间。
sentences.en_text: Then I counter with another reasonable argument: that a higher minimum wage will force businesses to employ fewer people for less time.

sentences.cn_text: 现在我们可以理解彼此的立场并认识到我们共同的价值观,因为我们都关心困难的劳动者。
sentences.en_text: Now we can understand each other’s positions and recognize our shared values, since we both care about needy workers.
